# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile facts yet, so I cannot safely choose a wire. I’m asking Mute to read the manual, establish a compact gesture code with Deaf, and relay Deaf’s visual observations to me. I use my gesture channel to signal cooperation/requesting a report, though the spoken request is the reliable message.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have found no tactile facts yet. Please read the manual and establish a clear small gesture code with Deaf for reporting the display, light, and wire markings. Then relay Deaf's observations and the required safe action to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible bomb state: display 3. Indicator light is green. Wires, left to right: wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue. Mute is consulting the manual and will give you the exact action.

I now know the visible state through Deaf’s report: display 3, green indicator, and wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. I still do not know which wire the manual specifies, so I will ask Mute for the exact cut instruction and will not act yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 3, green indicator, and wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. What exact wire does the manual require me to cut?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The visible state is unchanged: display 3, green light, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Do not act on gestures; wait for Mute's spoken manual instruction.

Mute’s manual instruction has not arrived, and Deaf confirms the bomb state is unchanged. Since the correct wire cannot be inferred safely from the visual state alone, I will not cut anything. I’ll request the manual’s instruction again and wait.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still need the manual's exact instruction: which wire position, 1, 2, or 3, should I cut for display 3 and green light?")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No verified manual instruction has reached me. Do not cut, press, or move anything until Mute explicitly states the required action in words and numbers.

The required manual instruction is still absent, so no wire is safe to cut. I am sending Mute a direct request for the exact action in words and a wire number; until that arrives, I will wait.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the manual result now, explicitly: cut wire 1, cut wire 2, or cut wire 3. Do not send a gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has not provided a spoken instruction. Do not act yet; wait for an explicit manual-based instruction naming the wire or action.

Mute’s explicit manual instruction still has not reached me. The bomb remains unchanged, and cutting any wire without the manual’s rule would be unsafe. I will request the instruction once more and take no action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="No manual instruction has reached me after several turns. Please send the exact safe action in plain words, including the wire number, on your next turn.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I am establishing a code with Mute: thumbs up means wire 1, victory means wire 2, I-love-you means wire 3. Thumbs down means cut; OK means leave it. Wait for Mute's coded instruction, which I will relay.

The code Deaf describes is now established, but it is not yet the manual’s instruction. I still need Mute to state the coded wire and whether to cut or leave it. I will not touch the bomb until that complete instruction arrives.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please send the complete coded instruction now: thumbs up, victory, or I-love-you for the wire, and thumbs down to cut or OK to leave.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has signaled ?, but that is not a valid coded instruction. Do not act. I have requested a wire symbol followed by cut or leave.

The received signal is invalid and gives no wire or action. I will not guess or cut anything. Mute must provide a valid manual-based instruction naming one wire and whether to cut it; I will wait for that instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your last signal was invalid. Send, in plain words, exactly one complete instruction: cut wire 1, cut wire 2, cut wire 3, or leave it.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's coded instruction is: cut wire 1. Wire 1 is the red wire. Cut only the red wire.

The manual-based instruction relayed by Deaf is explicit: cut wire 1, which is the red wire. I will perform only that specified action.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
